LESSON · 02 / 03 · FLYWIRE V783

Give the model a taste. Then check its answer.

The research question is whether activating sugar-sensing neurons predicts downstream responses involved in feeding. This page supplies an imposed sugar input and exposes the model's aggregate and watched-cell spikes. It refuses to call those spikes “feeding” until the pinned release has a verified cell-identity map.

← Back to the first experiment

PAPER-GROUNDED INPUT · NOT YET A VALIDATED OUTPUT CLAIM

Can sugar input change the downstream pattern?

The full FlyWire model is large: loading it is optional and desktop-first. Start with sugar off, record a baseline, then turn sugar on and compare conditions. The current committed build knows the input switch and spike monitor, but it does not yet ship the verified named sugar-sensory or MN9 index map from the paper's experiment.

What counts as evidence here?

A change in aggregate activity is an observation. A claim about a named feeding output requires the correct pinned cell identities and a preregistered comparison.

OBSERVATION API

Watch a bounded set.

Enter model neuron indices once a verified release mapping exists. At most 64 IDs are watched, and the interface reads the existing spike monitor without asking the model to materialize the whole brain.

No named cell map is bundled yet.

The field is intentionally raw: a number in this WASM build is not automatically a biological identity.

INTERPRETATION

What this page can and cannot say.

  • Can say: whether the imposed input changed the model's emitted spike pattern.
  • Can say: which watched indices emitted spikes during a run.
  • Cannot yet say: that a watched index is sugar-sensing or MN9 without a verified mapping.
  • Cannot say: that a simulated spike is a complete feeding behavior.
